dimensions.label: Motion adherence
evidence: I wanted to pick up there and show you where Olly fits into that specific problem
dimensions.tip: Even in a follow-up, ask a fresh discovery question before pivoting into product benefits to confirm nothing has changed.

dimensions.label: Discovery quality
evidence: We've got about 40 caregivers in the field and half of them are great about notes, half of them just write "client fine" and move on.
dimensions.tip: Dig deeper into timeline, budget, and decision process (e.g., 'what's driving urgency now, who else needs to sign off, what's your timeframe') instead of moving straight to product pitch.

dimensions.label: Talk / listen balance
dimensions.tip: Aim for more listening — open with questions and let the buyer talk.

dimensions.label: Buying-signal detection & handling
evidence: I'd want my ops manager in on that conversation too, she's the one who'd actually be living in this day to day.
dimensions.tip: Qualify this signal by asking about budget authority, timeline for decision, and whether other vendors are being evaluated.

dimensions.label: Objection handling
evidence: We tried a different monitoring tool two years ago and it just became noise... I don't want to add something that creates more work.
dimensions.tip: After addressing the noise objection, ask the prospect to reflect back whether that resolves their concern before moving to close.

dimensions.label: Proof-point fidelity
evidence: Agencies using it have seen about 35% more billable hours
dimensions.tip: Continue citing only published figures like this; consider adding source context (e.g., 'in our published case studies') for extra credibility.

dimensions.label: Next-step specificity
evidence: I'll follow up with you early next week to find a time that works for both of you.
dimensions.tip: Lock a specific date/time on the call itself rather than deferring scheduling to a follow-up email.
